subject.title: exec tool-error warnings bypass the exec suppression branch via the mutating-tool check (2026.7.1)

question: Should user-visible warnings for exec-like tools follow the command-result outcome or a richer read-only-shell classification, while retaining a visible failure signal for genuinely mutating shell actions?
rationale: The current classifier intentionally fails closed for shell syntax it cannot safely parse, but reusing that conservative recovery classification for user warnings creates the reported false-positive path. Choosing the acceptable visibility boundary is a product and safety-policy decision.

options.title: Separate warning classification
options.body: Define a narrow warning classifier for exec results and add regression coverage for benign non-zero read-only shell commands while preserving warnings for confirmed mutating actions.

options.title: Preserve fail-closed warnings
options.body: Keep current behavior for syntactically complex exec commands and document that their warning visibility is intentional until reliable command semantics are available.

options.title: Use result status only
options.body: Suppress warning payloads when the tool result contract says `completed`, even if an exit code is non-zero, after confirming that contract across all exec backends.

recommendation.title: Separate warning classification
recommendation.body: Define a narrow warning classifier for exec results and add regression coverage for benign non-zero read-only shell commands while preserving warnings for confirmed mutating actions.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily concerns the current payload warning policy, with mutation-classification input from Swader.
